surfBiteReport: The most current readable report for this stretch of Florida Panhandle Gulf-front coast is from noeoutdoors.com/pcb, dated roughly three to four weeks ago (late July 2026), so treat it as recent-but-not-this-week. Along the beaches from Panama City Beach through the 30A corridor, the surf was producing Spanish mackerel, whiting, redfish, and jack crevalle, with action concentrated in the first and second troughs rather than at maximum casting distance — watching for birds and jumping baitfish helped anglers pick the right spots. Water temperature is 85°F. Sand fleas are a reliable and abundant surf bait right now if you can rake them out of the wash, and they've been the go-to for pompano and whiting in clear, non-grassy stretches of beach. Bluefish and Spanish mackerel have also been showing up opportunistically, especially when bait schools move through; a fast-moving lure kept ready alongside live or cut bait is a smart two-pronged approach for this time of year.
